# Extensions and skills

The 12 first-party extensions in this repository, what each provides, and every skill
they ship. A project uses an extension by installing its package and listing it in
`extensions` in `protoboard.config.ts`; a capability provider is also loaded when a module's
`<capability>.config.ts` names it. In a project, `protoboard doctor` lists what is configured,
`protoboard skills` the skills, `protoboard capabilities` the providers, and `protoboard evals --list`
the eval cases. Writing a provider: [the provider guide](../guides/writing-a-capability-provider.md).

## Capability providers

| Capability | Provider | Native folder | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cad` | `@protoboardai/ext-enclosure-cad` | `build123d/` | Enclosures (cases, caps, back covers) with build123d: generated from the features they provide and what goes inside them |
| `cad` | `@protoboardai/ext-frame-cad` | `frame-cad/` | Plates (frames, top plates, brackets) from a module's UHD bolt patterns and frames, and nominal mounting-hardware bodies (screws, nuts, standoffs, spacers) from their sizes, with build123d; DXF cutting profiles for plates |
| `cad` | `@protoboardai/ext-harness-cad` | `harness-cad/` | Routed wire harnesses: an obstacle-free route through the assembled model, swept conductors, plug housings and solder joints (build123d) |
| `cad` | `@protoboardai/ext-parts` | `part-cad/` | A project-researched part's body drawn by its own build123d script (parts/local/<id>/part-cad/<script>.py): run, recorded and exported as STEP, GLB and a feature manifest |
| `circuit` | `@protoboardai/ext-tscircuit` | `tscircuit/` | PCBs from UHD boards with tscircuit: generated source, local autorouting, Gerber/BOM/PnP/GLB/STEP/manifest/netlist and SVG renders, DRC and netlist drift |
| `firmware` | `@protoboardai/ext-esp-idf` | `esp-idf/` | ESP-IDF 5.3 board_pins.h (buses, addresses, buttons, controls, wake mask) and sdkconfig.defaults (target, flash, console, RTC clock) for an ESP32-C3 board |
| `firmware` | `@protoboardai/ext-zephyr` | `zephyr/` | Zephyr 4.2 board definition (board.yml, Kconfig, defconfig, devicetree, pinctrl) and a Kconfig fragment for an nRF52840 board |

## Skills

Start with **build-a-project**: it takes an agent from a brief to a release and delegates to the others.
`protoboard skills export --host all` puts them where an agent finds them (`claude-code`: `.claude/skills/`; `agents-md`: a list in `AGENTS.md`); a project made by `protoboard init` runs it at the end of `npm install`.

## Extensions

### @protoboardai/ext-docs

Technical documents (datasheet, assembly guide) for a project's system: every value a query into the UHD model, figures rendered from the CAD artifacts, stand-in test data watermarked until measured data replaces it, and a verifier. Version 0.2.3; source [packages/ext-docs](../../packages/ext-docs).

Compatibility: `protoboard ^0.2.0`, `uhd >=0.3.0`.

| Operation | Effect | Needs | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tech-docs` | export | `chrome` | Build the datasheet and assembly guide (HTML, PDF, bound values) for the project's root system from its model, CAD artifacts and docs/docspec.ts; stand-in test data is refreshed, measured data kept |
| `tech-docs-verify` | export | `chrome`, `poppler` | Verify the built documents against the live model: values, units, placeholders, stand-in marks, images, layout, typography, BOM, assembly coverage; fails on any error |
| `package:spec` | pure | — | Manufacturing Package: what is made for each unit (boards, mechanical parts, cables) from the providers' standard outputs, with figures from their GLBs |
| `package:assembly` | pure | — | Manufacturing Package: each unit's assembly guide: tools, kit with thumbnails, one illustrated step per planned step (exploded mates, routed cables), connections, torques, coverage |

| Tool | Purpose | Runtime |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `chrome` | A Chromium-family browser (Google Chrome, Chromium, Microsoft Edge or Brave), run headless: the datasheet and the assembly guide are laid out, their figures drawn and the PDFs printed with it | — |
| `poppler` | poppler-utils: pdfinfo, pdffonts (document checks) and pdftoppm (review page images) | — |

Skills: `uhd-tech-docs`, `uhd-tech-docs-verify`.

Eval cases: `build-datasheet` (Build and verify the quadcopter's datasheet).

### @protoboardai/ext-drone

Multirotor domain pack: flight-controller configuration (Betaflight) generated from the UHD model. Version 0.2.3; source [packages/ext-drone](../../packages/ext-drone).

Compatibility: `protoboard ^0.2.0`, `uhd >=0.3.0`.

| Operation | Effect | Needs | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `betaflight-cli` | export | — | Generate a Betaflight CLI dump (serial ports, receiver, OSD/VTX, GPS, compass) from the model's links; every line cites its link or part fact |
| `package:work-order` | pure | — | Manufacturing Package: the flight-controller configuration (file and loading steps) in the root unit's work order; refuses a configuration that no longer matches the model |
| `package:test-plan` | pure | — | Manufacturing Package: the props-off bench check of the flight controller in the root unit's test plan |

Skills: `firmware-config`, `firmware-verify`.

Eval cases: `gps-moved-to-uart3` (Update the flight-controller configuration after the GPS moved to UART3).

### @protoboardai/ext-enclosure-cad

Enclosure CAD: a printed or machined case generated with build123d from the UHD features it must provide (openings, plungers, windows, light pipes, insert bosses, O-ring glands, threads, strap lugs, the lid joint) and the bodies the assembly places inside it; fit, wall, seal and alignment checks. Version 0.2.3; source [packages/ext-enclosure-cad](../../packages/ext-enclosure-cad).

Compatibility: `protoboard ^0.2.0`, `uhd >=0.3.0`.

**Capability `cad`**: Enclosures (cases, caps, back covers) with build123d: generated from the features they provide and what goes inside them. Operations `cad:generate`, `cad:export`, `cad:extract`, `cad:check`. Constraints: `wall_mm` (required), `floor_mm`, `lid_mm`, `clearance_mm`, `clearance_top_mm`, `min_wall_mm`, `material`, `shape`, `cavity_mm`, `split_z_mm`, `joint`, `fasteners`, `exclude`, `resolution_mm`.

| Operation | Effect | Needs | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `package:work-order` | pure | — | Manufacturing Package: the print order of each printed enclosure (material, profile, each part's orientation and supports, inserts, O-rings, plungers, lid screws) |
| `package:test-plan` | pure | — | Manufacturing Package: the enclosure's checks (seal squeeze, buttons, plugs, lid joint, tight fits) from its build report |

| Tool | Purpose | Runtime |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `python-build123d` | Python with build123d, numpy and scipy (enclosure generator; the fit analysis uses ext-harness-cad's voxel clearance field) | `cad` (python): `build123d==0.13.0` `numpy==2.5.3` `scipy==1.18.1` |

Skills: `enclosure-cad`.

### @protoboardai/ext-esp-idf

firmware provider: ESP-IDF pin and peripheral header and sdkconfig.defaults for ESP32-C3 modules, every setting citing the UHD facts it comes from. Version 0.2.3; source [packages/ext-esp-idf](../../packages/ext-esp-idf).

Compatibility: `protoboard ^0.2.0`, `uhd >=0.3.0`.

**Capability `firmware`**: ESP-IDF 5.3 board_pins.h (buses, addresses, buttons, controls, wake mask) and sdkconfig.defaults (target, flash, console, RTC clock) for an ESP32-C3 board. Operations `firmware:generate`, `firmware:export`, `firmware:extract`, `firmware:check`. Constraints: `controller`, `console`, `i2c_frequency_hz`, `uart_baud`, `wake`.

Skills: `firmware-config-esp-idf`.

Eval cases: `wake-on-fuel-gauge` (Configure ESP-IDF for the bottle cap after a wake source was asked for on a pin that cannot wake the chip).

### @protoboardai/ext-frame-cad

Custom structure and hardware CAD: plates generated from a module's UHD bolt patterns and frames, and nominal fastener bodies from their sizes, both as a provider of the cad capability (build123d), with STEP/GLB/DXF exports, feature manifests, frame and staleness checks and explicit re-binding. Version 0.2.3; source [packages/ext-frame-cad](../../packages/ext-frame-cad).

Compatibility: `protoboard ^0.2.0`, `uhd >=0.3.0`.

**Capability `cad`**: Plates (frames, top plates, brackets) from a module's UHD bolt patterns and frames, and nominal mounting-hardware bodies (screws, nuts, standoffs, spacers) from their sizes, with build123d; DXF cutting profiles for plates. Operations `cad:generate`, `cad:export`, `cad:extract`, `cad:check`. Constraints: `margin_mm`, `corner_radius_mm`, `arm_width_mm`, `arm_slot_width_mm`, `hub_extra_mm`, `pad_margin_mm`, `pad_height_mm`, `pad_center_relief_mm`, `hole_clearance_mm`, `clamp_wall_mm`, `clamp_margin_mm`, `clamp_height_mm`, `pads`, `outline_mm`, `slots_mm`.

| Operation | Effect | Needs | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `frame-cad` | export | `python-build123d` | Alias of cad:generate then cad:export for every plate module (or the named ones), each bound by its cad.config.ts; returns the new signatures and any stale bindings |
| `frame-cad-rebind` | export | — | Copy the exported signatures (out/body.manifest.json) and generated frame origins (frame-cad/frames.json) into the module source (explicit re-binding after a reviewed change); prints every change |
| `hardware-cad` | export | `python-build123d` | Alias of cad:generate then cad:export for every mounting-hardware module (screws, nuts, standoffs, spacers; or the named ones), each bound by its cad.config.ts: nominal STEP, GLB and manifest with volume from its UHD sizes; returns each volume and the one it replaces |
| `package:work-order` | pure | — | Manufacturing Package: the cut order of each plate in its unit's work order (process, material, stock, quantities by DXF layer, hole sizes, router bit, edge finish) |
| `package:test-plan` | pure | — | Manufacturing Package: inspection of what the cut order asks for (hole sizes, edges, edge distance) |

| Check | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `frames` | Plate modules that no cad.config.ts binds to this provider (each bound module's frames and staleness are its cad:check) |
| `hardware` | Mounting-hardware modules that no cad.config.ts binds to this provider (each bound module's stale sizes and export are its cad:check) |

| Tool | Purpose | Runtime |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `python-build123d` | Python with build123d (CAD kernel for the plate generator) | `cad` (python): `build123d==0.13.0` |

Skills: `frame-cad`, `frame-cad-verify`.

Eval cases: `regenerate-after-vtx-move` (Regenerate the frame's CAD after the transmission module mount moved 5 mm back).

### @protoboardai/ext-hardware

General hardware engineering: system composition and review, harnesses and fastener stack-ups, test and measurement, BOM export, evidence coverage. Releases are @protoboardai/ext-release. Version 0.2.3; source [packages/ext-hardware](../../packages/ext-hardware).

Compatibility: `protoboard ^0.2.0`, `uhd >=0.3.0`.

| Operation | Effect | Needs | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bom` | export | — | Write the bill of materials (quantities multiplied through the instance tree, with origins) to docs/bom.md and docs/bom.json |

| Check | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `evidence` | Every purchased part used has cited sources and a recorded verification |

Skills: `build-a-project`, `system-compose`, `system-review`, `harness-author`, `harness-verify`, `test-and-measure`.

Eval cases: `compose-probe-cable` (Compose the temperature probe's connection through its cable to the cap board); `e2e-desk-rover` (End to end: a small project from its brief to a Manufacturing Package); `find-reversed-cell-leads` (Find the cell leads soldered the wrong way round, with the scenario that describes it hidden); `fix-gnss-uart-swap` (Find and fix a GNSS lead soldered with RX and TX swapped); `fix-two-wiring-faults` (Find and fix two wiring faults at once: the O4 powered from the pack, and the GNSS RX and TX swapped); `rough-draft-is-concept` (A rough draft is the concept level: three to six blocks, and a question before going deeper); `tidy-the-diagram` (The diagram reads before the build is done: no strip of parts, nothing on top of anything, measured and looked at).

### @protoboardai/ext-harness-cad

Routed wire-harness CAD (a provider of the cad capability): each cable's 3D geometry (conductors swept along an obstacle-free route, twisted where the cable is, connector housings and solder joints) generated from the assembled UHD model and bound to the frames its ends land on. Version 0.2.3; source [packages/ext-harness-cad](../../packages/ext-harness-cad).

Compatibility: `protoboard ^0.2.0`, `uhd >=0.3.0`.

**Capability `cad`**: Routed wire harnesses: an obstacle-free route through the assembled model, swept conductors, plug housings and solder joints (build123d). Operations `cad:generate`, `cad:export`, `cad:extract`, `cad:check`.

| Operation | Effect | Needs | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `harness-cad` | export | `python-build123d` | Alias of cad:generate then cad:export for every wire harness (or the named ones), each bound by its cad.config.ts, in one routing run |
| `package:work-order` | pure | — | Manufacturing Package: preparation of each routed cable in its unit's work order (cut length, strip, conductors, lay, bend radius, terminations) |
| `package:test-plan` | pure | — | Manufacturing Package: routing checks of each cable (bend radius, clearance, slack) |

| Check | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `routes` | Wire harnesses that no cad.config.ts binds to a cad provider (each bound harness's route report is its cad:check) |

| Tool | Purpose | Runtime |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `python-build123d` | Python with build123d, numpy and scipy (voxel routing, sweeps, STEP/GLB export) | `cad` (python): `build123d==0.13.0` `numpy==2.5.3` `scipy==1.18.1` |

Skills: `harness-cad`.

Eval cases: `reroute-after-vtx-move` (Re-route the cable whose part moved: the DJI O4 lead after the transmission module moved 5 mm back).

### @protoboardai/ext-parts

Purchased parts as datasheet-honest UHD definitions: research and cite the sources, author the ModuleDef, verify it automatically and by an independent audit, record the verification. Works on a project's parts (parts/local, parts/evidence) and on the cloud part library (library/parts). Version 0.2.3; source [packages/ext-parts](../../packages/ext-parts).

Compatibility: `protoboard ^0.2.0`, `uhd >=0.3.0`.

**Capability `cad`**: A project-researched part's body drawn by its own build123d script (parts/local/<id>/part-cad/<script>.py): run, recorded and exported as STEP, GLB and a feature manifest. Operations `cad:generate`, `cad:export`, `cad:extract`, `cad:check`. Constraints: `generator`.

| Operation | Effect | Needs | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `part-verify` | pure | — | Automated checks for one local purchased part (metadata, citations, structure, parameters, vocabulary, connectors, pins, CAD) and pair DRC against mates; fails on any error |
| `part-verification` | export | — | Write parts/evidence/<id>/verification.json from the audit and gaps in .research/ and the part's assumption traits |

| Tool | Purpose | Runtime |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `python-build123d` | Python with build123d (CAD kernel the project's part-body scripts run on) | `cad` (python): `build123d==0.13.0` |

Skills: `uhd-authoring`, `uhd-part-research`, `uhd-part-author`, `uhd-part-verify`.

Eval cases: `author-ldo-regulator` (Author a small purchased part (an LDO regulator) from datasheet excerpts and pass verification).

### @protoboardai/ext-release

Releases: `protoboard release` refuses a project with check errors, stale outputs or uncommitted changes, then writes the Manufacturing Package (overview, per-unit spec sheet, BOM and ordering list, work order, assembly guide and test plan, manufacturing files, index.html) and a reproducible release manifest. Version 0.2.3; source [packages/ext-release](../../packages/ext-release).

Compatibility: `protoboard ^0.2.0`, `uhd >=0.3.0`.

| Operation | Effect | Needs | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `release` | export | `chrome` | Write the Manufacturing Package to release/<version>/ (units from release.units; one folder per unit) with its manifest, after checking the project is clean |
| `package:spec` | pure | — | Spec sheet: what the unit is, key figures, contents, interfaces (from the model) |
| `package:bom` | pure | — | Bill of materials: the unit's module breakdown (bom.csv); the root also gets the whole-product ordering list (ordering-list.csv) |
| `package:work-order` | pure | — | Work order: ordering checklist, fabrication orders per custom part, assembly operations from the model |
| `package:assembly` | pure | — | Assembly guide: kit and one step per joint the unit makes |
| `package:test-plan` | pure | — | Test plan: first-article inspection, fits and joints, records to capture |

| Tool | Purpose | Runtime |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `chrome` | A Chromium-family browser (Google Chrome, Chromium, Microsoft Edge or Brave), run headless: the package's documents are laid out, their figures drawn and the PDFs printed with it, through @protoboardai/ext-docs' renderer | — |

Skills: `release`.

Eval cases: `release-after-hand-edit` (Cut a release of the smart bottle after a generated file was edited by hand).

### @protoboardai/ext-sourcing

Part sourcing: external discovery, datasheet facts with checked quotes, supplier and lifecycle observations as dated evidence (never orders), alternates, and handoff into locally authored UHD parts. Version 0.2.3; source [packages/ext-sourcing](../../packages/ext-sourcing).

Compatibility: `protoboard ^0.2.0`, `uhd >=0.3.0`.

| Check | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| `sourcing` | Sourcing records are dated and sourced, carry no orders or credentials, and state single-source, low-stock and lifecycle disqualifiers unless a named person accepted the risk |

| Tool | Purpose | Runtime |
| --- | --- | --- |
